niche.title: They Wanted The To Die - Tuskegee Experiment
niche.description:
The Tuskegee Syphilis Study was a 40-year U.S. Public Health Service study involving Black men in Macon County, Alabama. The men were not infected with syphilis by the government, but many were deceived about the purpose of the study and were not given effective treatment once penicillin became available.

This video looks at how the study began, why it continued for so long, the role of Nurse Eunice Rivers, how the story was exposed in 1972, and the lasting impact Tuskegee had on medical ethics, informed consent, and trust in the healthcare system.

niche.title: Why a Baby Won't Stop Crying 😰
niche.description: Sometimes a baby who cries and won't settle has a single hair (or a thread) wrapped tight around a toe or finger. As the toe swells, the hair tightens and sinks into the skin, and it can cut off the toe's blood supply. Doctors call it a hair tourniquet. Often the crying is the only sign. If a baby can't be settled, undress them and check every toe, every finger and the genitals for a hair or thread.
